_comment: NOT A SIGNOFF SPEC. This file exists only to reproduce klayout-tools
upstream issue #2169 -- `klt erc`'s `ties[]` (`erc.missing_tie`)
collapsing a real routed standard-cell layout's connectivity and
reporting a FALSE `erc.supply_short`. Its committed report
(`erc_reports/tmds_encoder_tie_known_gap.erc.json`) is evidence OF the
tool gap, not evidence ABOUT this design. Do not cite its zero
erc.missing_tie count as a well-tie verdict: that zero is produced by
the same collapse that produces the false short (every tap trivially
reaches the declared net once the whole design is one island).
klt erc layout/gds/tmds_encoder.gds \
layout/erc-tie-spec.known-gap.json --format json
Identical to `erc-supply-spec.json` except for the `ties[]` section
below. gf180mcu draws both wells for this cell library, so both tie
checks are individually well-posed: Nwell 21/0 is the n-well, LVPWELL
204/0 is the low-voltage p-well (named in the PDK's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp, gf180mcuD), and Contact 33/0 is
the tap contact that ties each well up to its own supply rail on
Metal1 -- which exists at all because flow/pnr_tmds_encoder.py runs
tapcell -distance 100 -tapcell_master gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__filltie
(filltie instances draw exactly the two taps these entries expect).
`tap_layer` is Contact rather than a diffusion or implant layer because
the tap gf180mcu actually draws is a boolean (`Comp n Nplus` inside
Nwell, `Comp n Pplus` inside LVPWELL) that this spec grammar cannot
express -- see klayout-tools#2169 and gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION
F-034, where Comp 22/0, Nplus 32/0 and Contact 33/0 were each measured
separately and all three collapse the design identically.
